title: A counterexample to Naimark's problem in ZFC
coverage:
I read every section in full: introduction, states, hnn, bridge, iteration and construction (build/sections/*.tex).

States section checked: decreasing excision, including the approximate-identity estimate and the uniqueness of h on N via one-vector Kadison transitivity and the open mapping theorem; projection excision; cross-excision (pi_h^{**}(r_k)=0 and the y^2<=y<=y_{nu0} bound); trace-null supports; the peaking-sequence expectation (continuity at infinity, bimodularity, trace preservation); and simplicity from (U) plus a faithful expectation.

HNN section checked: the amalgamated free product module, P_F compression and the faithful trace; the M_2 corner identities v*v=vv*=e_1 and v d v*=theta(d), worked by hand; the reduced-word coefficient table; uniqueness via the moment-norm formula; restriction; the reorder proposition (freeness over O and the symmetric moment recursion); and the limit lemma.

Bridge checked: the module bound ||dP_G||<=||E(d*d)||^{1/2}; the identity (1-P_G)w(1-P_G)=0; the endpoint decay via normal extensions, trace-null and Dini; the transfer identities P^{l(b)}b=bP^{r(b)} under the theta^{-1}-twisted embedding; every case of the core-disappearance analysis (m=1, m=2 with both ends matched, and m>=3); uniqueness and no-other-join through GNS-vector fixing; and the corner descent with the designated join via Ad v.

Iteration checked: dependency-closedness of j∪(S∩β); the induction showing the omitted pair stays inequivalent, using the bridge's no-other-join clause; uniqueness of trace-preserving expectations used to match data for the reorder; countable determination; and the state count of at most c.

Construction checked: the schedule injection on c^+ x c^+; the use of KOS on separable simple A[S]; the trace of q_n=gamma(p_n) via the unique trace on matrix subalgebras; peaking lifted through (U); and that every final pure state is caught because countable subsets of c^+ are bounded.

No computations needed sympy beyond hand-checking the matrix identities.
main_claim: In ZFC there is a unital, infinite-dimensional, simple C*-algebra with a faithful tracial state whose nonzero irreducible representations are all unitarily equivalent. This is a counterexample to Naimark's problem that needs no diamond principle. It is built as a length-c^+ iteration of reduced HNN "bridges" over the CAR algebra, using countable determination of pure states.
